chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to him: Blood may be on the garment while I am in salat (prayer). He said: If you see it and you are wearing another garment besides it, then cast it off and perform salat (prayer). But if you have no other garment on you, then continue in your salat (prayer), and there is no repetition required of you so long as it does not exceed the measure of a dirham. If it is less than that, then it is nothing, whether you saw it or did not see it. But if you had seen it and it was more than the measure of a dirham, and you neglected washing it and performed many prayers in it, then repeat what you performed in it.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or clothing worn in salat (prayer)
key_terms.غَسْلَهُ: washing the blood from the garment
key_terms.مِقْدَارِ الدِّرْهَمِ: the legal measure used here as the threshold for excused blood

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying with blood on one's clothing if it is less than or more than a dirham?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about blood on a garment during salat (prayer). It distinguishes between a small amount and an amount exceeding the measure of a dirham, and also addresses whether the person noticed it and whether another garment was available.
